note: Draft content for frontend use. Have an agronomist / Coffee Board guidance verify chemical names and doses before production.

items.name: Coffee White Stem Borer (CWSB)
symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of leaves, followed by drying of the branch or whole plant
Ridges or tunnels under the bark of the main stem near the collar
Dry sawdust-like frass and small oval exit holes on the stem
White grub (larva) found inside the stem when it is split

severity_levels.low: A few plants show early yellowing, with egg-laying or ridges on the bark but no exit holes yet
severity_levels.medium: Several plants with exit holes and wilting branches
severity_levels.high: Many plants dying; infestation visible across the block

items.destroy_guidance: Uproot plants with confirmed borer damage (exit holes or grubs inside the stem) and burn them, including roots, so that grubs and pupae are killed. Do this before the next flight season. Do not leave cut stems or stumps lying in the plantation.
immediate_actions: Scout all plants in the block, especially the stem from the collar up to the first branches
Uproot and burn the heavily infested plants, including roots
Cut and burn dried infested branches, and do not leave them in the field
Scrape loose bark gently and apply stem treatment recommended by the Coffee Board on remaining plants
Mark the block as affected and re-scout after 2 weeks
cultural_control: Maintain adequate shade, because thin shade increases CWSB incidence
Avoid water stress and delayed or missed blossom and backing irrigation
Remove and burn infested plants before the flight season starts
Prefer CWSB-tolerant selections at replanting (for example S.4595 and Sln.11)
items.chemical_control: Use only the stem treatment / insecticide recommended by the Coffee Board for your region, following the label for dose, timing and pre-harvest interval.

risk_season.trigger: Adult beetle flight begins after pre-monsoon showers and lasts through the early monsoon. Dry spells during this period raise the risk.

items.fertilizer_note: Fertilizer does not control the borer. Do not apply extra nitrogen to infested plants.
items.irrigation_note: Keep soil moisture steady. Water-stressed plants are more attractive to the beetle.
items.escalate_when: Infestation spreads to new plants after removal, or more than about 5 percent of plants in a block are affected. Contact the Coffee Board extension officer or CCRI.

items.name: Coffee Leaf Rust
symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaf
Orange powdery spore masses on the underside of the leaf
Spots merge, leaves turn brown and fall prematurely
Severe defoliation and die-back of branches in bad outbreaks

severity_levels.low: Few leaves with spots, mainly in the lower canopy
severity_levels.medium: Many leaves with orange pustules and some leaf fall
severity_levels.high: Heavy leaf fall and exposed branches

items.destroy_guidance: Do not uproot the plant. Remove and destroy only badly affected leaves and shoots, and do not leave fallen infected leaves piled under the plant.
immediate_actions: Look for orange pustules on the underside of the leaf
Spray copper-based fungicide (Bordeaux mixture or copper oxychloride) as per Coffee Board schedule
Regulate shade and prune to improve airflow
Improve drainage in wet patches
Re-scout after 14 days
cultural_control: Prune and handle shade before and during the monsoon
Plant rust-resistant varieties at replanting (for example Cauvery, Chandragiri, Sln.9)
Keep plants well nourished and avoid heavy overbearing
items.chemical_control: Follow the Coffee Board spray schedule for copper-based and systemic fungicides, and apply in dry weather windows only.

risk_season.trigger: Spread is fastest during humid, rainy weather, and the main outbreak peaks after the monsoon.

items.fertilizer_note: Fertilizer does not cure rust. Avoid heavy nitrogen during an outbreak, and if the plants look weak, do a soil test and use balanced nutrition after recovery.
items.irrigation_note: Avoid wetting the leaves. Do not cut water, because stressed plants lose more leaves.
items.escalate_when: Heavy leaf fall spreads to more than about 25 percent of the block or does not slow after spraying.

items.name: Coffee Berry Borer
symptoms: Tiny bore hole at the tip of the berry
Berries drop prematurely or beans inside are damaged
Powdery frass inside the berry and chewed beans

severity_levels.low: Under about 2 percent of berries bored
severity_levels.medium: About 2 to 5 percent of berries bored
severity_levels.high: More than 5 percent of berries bored

items.destroy_guidance: Do not uproot. Strip off and destroy all remaining berries after harvest, including those on the ground.
immediate_actions: Pick all ripe berries on time and do not leave over-ripe fruit on the plant
Remove and destroy dropped and left-over berries (use hot water or deep burying)
Check berries from several plants to estimate the percentage bored
Use traps if available, as recommended by the Coffee Board
cultural_control: Clean harvesting with no left-over berries in the field
Keep drying yards and stores clean of old infested beans
items.chemical_control: Use only Coffee Board approved options, and only when needed.

risk_season.trigger: Beetles breed in left-over berries and spread during and after harvest.

items.escalate_when: More than 5 percent of berries are bored after sanitation.

items.name: Brown Eye Spot
symptoms: Round brown spots with a grey or white centre and a yellow halo on the leaf
Dark, sunken patches on berries
More common on plants that are stressed or poorly nourished

severity_levels.low: Scattered spots on a few leaves
severity_levels.medium: Many spots and some leaf fall

items.destroy_guidance: Do not uproot. In nurseries, remove and destroy badly affected seedlings.
immediate_actions: Improve plant health, since this disease mostly hits weak plants
Regulate shade and ensure proper drainage
Spray copper fungicide if the infection is spreading, as per Coffee Board guidance
Use balanced nutrition if the plants show weak growth
items.chemical_control: Copper-based fungicide as per Coffee Board guidance.

risk_season.trigger: Warm and humid weather, or plants weakened by drought or poor nutrition.

items.fertilizer_note: Weak or poorly fed plants are more prone. Fix the cause with a soil test and balanced nutrition, not extra nitrogen.
items.irrigation_note: Keep moisture steady and avoid water stress.
items.escalate_when: Spread continues after correcting stress and spraying.

items.name: Black Rot
symptoms: Leaves and berries turn black and hang on the plant, stuck by fungal threads
Rotting of berries and leaves, mostly in the wet season
Affected leaves and berries do not fall off easily

severity_levels.low: A few shoots or leaves affected
severity_levels.medium: Several branches with hanging blackened leaves or berries
severity_levels.high: Large areas of the canopy affected

items.destroy_guidance: Do not uproot. Remove and burn the hanging blackened leaves and berries.
immediate_actions: Pick off and destroy infected leaves, berries and twigs
Open the canopy by pruning and regulating shade
Spray Bordeaux mixture or copper fungicide as per Coffee Board guidance, in the early monsoon
cultural_control: Prune before the monsoon to reduce humidity inside the canopy
items.chemical_control: Copper-based fungicide as per Coffee Board guidance.

risk_season.trigger: Continuous wet weather and high humidity with dense canopy.

items.fertilizer_note: Fertilizer does not treat black rot.
items.escalate_when: Spread continues into the next rains despite pruning and spraying.

items.name: Root Rot
items.scientific_name: Various fungi (for example Fusarium, Rosellinia, Armillaria)
symptoms: Sudden wilting and yellowing of the whole plant
Rotten, dark or discoloured roots and collar
Plants die in patches, often in waterlogged areas

severity_levels.high: Spreading patches and many dead plants

items.destroy_guidance: Uproot dead and dying plants with confirmed root rot, including as many roots as possible, and burn them. Isolate the pit and avoid replanting in the same spot immediately.
immediate_actions: Check the roots and collar for rot and for stem borer
Uproot and burn affected plants
Improve drainage and avoid waterlogging
Drench the neighbouring plants as per Coffee Board guidance
cultural_control: Remove old stumps and roots from the plantation
items.chemical_control: Use only Coffee Board recommended drenches.
items.fertilizer_note: Fertilizer will not recover rotted roots.
items.irrigation_note: Reduce irrigation in the affected block and fix drainage.
items.escalate_when: Patches keep expanding after drainage is fixed.

items.name: Coffee Leaf Miner
symptoms: Irregular brown blotches on the upper side of the leaf
Tiny larvae feeding inside the leaf tissue
Leaf drop in severe infestations

severity_levels.medium: Many leaves mined with some leaf drop

items.destroy_guidance: Do not uproot the plant. Pick off and destroy severely mined leaves.
immediate_actions: Look for mined blotches and larvae inside the leaf
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays, which kill natural enemies
Spray only if infestation is severe, using a Coffee Board approved option
cultural_control: Maintain shade and avoid dry-spell stress
Keep field clean of weeds and fallen leaves
items.chemical_control: Only if severe, and only an option approved by the Coffee Board.
items.irrigation_note: Avoid prolonged water stress in dry spells.
items.escalate_when: Leaf drop is heavy across the block.
